Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines

crazy adjective

mad

also mad (insane), insane, madness, go crazy, you’re crazy, nuts, be crazy about

classical

Cic. Ac. 2.52 (Lewis & Short)
Hor. S. 2.6.29: quid tibi vīs, īnsāne?

īnsānus, īnsāna, īnsānum

mad, crazy

Unsound in mind, and in talk of anyone behaving wildly: “you madman!”. The verb īnsāniō, īnsānīre is to be mad, to act crazily; īnsānia is madness.

Other words

  • dēmēns, dēmentis — out of one’s mind; senseless

    also used · classical · Cic. N.D. 1.94: dēsipere, dēlīrāre, dēmentēs esse (Lewis & Short)

    Very common in Cicero, of a mind gone or a senseless act.

  • dēlīrus, dēlīra, dēlīrum — silly, doting, crazy

    also used · classical · Cic. de Or. 2.75: senex (Lewis & Short); Traupman 150, 298

    From dē līrā, out of the furrow; of an old man in his dotage, or anyone talking nonsense. The verb is dēlīrō.

  • cerrītus, cerrīta, cerrītum — cracked, crazy

    also used · classical · Plaut. Amph. 2.2.144 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 298

    (vōx cōmica: Plaut.; Hor. S. 2.3.278)

    Of a crazed brain. To be crazy about someone is dēperīre (Traupman 96: eam dēperit).

Examples

  • quid tibi vīs, īnsāne?

    what do you want, you madman?Hor. S. 2.6.29

  • īnsānīre libet quoniam tibi

    since you want to be crazyVerg. Ecl. 3.36

  • quidquid dēlīrant rēgēs, plectuntur Achīvī

    whatever madness the kings commit, it is the Greeks who payHor. Ep. 1.2.14

See also angry, mental.
